extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, patent attorneys/agents, and counsel involved in USPTO OED disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules applied in Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) disciplinary proceedings before a USPTO Administrative Law Judge, including conduct rules, service/answering requirements, and factors for imposing sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.36 — Requirement to answer complaint; consequences for failure
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to timely file an answer will constitute an admission of the allegations in the complaint and may result in entry of default judgment. 37 C.F.R. § 11.36(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a respondent does not answer the Complaint the respondent is deemed to have admitted the allegations; the decision recounts that Respondent failed to answer and was found in DEFAULT, and the Court adopted the allegations as findings of fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.35(a)(2)(i) — Service on respondent at address of record
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of the Complaint pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.35(a)(2)(i) by mailing via U.S. certified mail, return receipt requested, to the address provided by Respondent to OED.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of delivery (certified mail + USPS records) supports that service was effective; the decision relies on such delivery evidence when determining Respondent received the Complaint and subsequent notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.103 — Duty of reasonable diligence and promptness
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client. 37 C.F.R. § 11.103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example violation: agreeing to file a response to a Final Office Action by a date (Sept 10, 2013) and failing to file it, allowing an application to become abandoned and failing to attempt revival were held to violate § 11.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3) — Duty to keep client reasonably informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must keep the client reasonably informed about the status of a matter. 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to notify client that a response was not filed and that the application became abandoned constitutes a violation; the decision cites the respondent's failure to inform the client as a breach of this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(4) — Duty to promptly comply with reasonable requests for information
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must promptly comply with reasonable requests for information from the client. 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing misleading or incorrect information in response to client inquiries (e.g., stating 'everything is normal here' when the application was abandoned) is noncompliant and violates this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(d) — Prompt delivery of client funds or property
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must promptly deliver to a client any funds or property that the client is entitled to receive. 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: failing to return a client's prototype upon request after transfer of representation was found to violate § 11.115(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.116(d) — Surrender of papers/property and refund of unearned fees upon termination
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must surrender papers and property to which the client is entitled and refund any advance payment of fee or expense that has not been earned or incurred upon termination of the practitioner-client relationship. 37 C.F.R. § 11.116(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retaining prepaid fees ($1,500) when the agreed services were not performed and failing to return unearned fees after representation ended was a violation of § 11.116(d). The decision cites invoicing that misdescribed services as evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c) — Prohibition on dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation is proscribed. 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: sending an invoice implying that a response had been filed when it had not, and knowingly misrepresenting the status of the application to the client's son, were treated as dishonest or misleading conduct violating § 11.804(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.801(b) — Duty to respond to lawful disciplinary demands for information
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not knowingly fail to respond to lawful demands for information from a disciplinary authority. 37 C.F.R. § 11.801(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to answer OED's Request for Information and Evidence (RFI) and subsequent prompts, despite proof of receipt, constitutes a violation of § 11.801(b). The decision relied on certified-mail return receipts showing delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d) — Conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice is proscribed. 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A respondent's failure to respond to OED inquiries and cooperate with disciplinary processes was held to undermine public confidence and thus be prejudicial to the administration of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.22(f) — Request for Information and Evidence (RFI) procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: OED may send a Request for Information and Evidence under 37 C.F.R. § 11.22(f), providing a specified time period (e.g., 30 days) to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision describes an RFI sent with a 30-day response window (and a later Lack of Response letter providing additional time). Failure to respond to RFIs is a basis for disciplinary violation findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.43 — Motion for default judgment procedure and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: OED may file a Motion for Default Judgment and Imposition of Sanctions; counsel may notify respondent of intent to file such a motion per 37 C.F.R. § 11.43.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision notes counsel sent a certified-letter notice of intent to move for default; proper notice and opportunity to respond are part of the procedural framework leading to a default judgment when respondent does not answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file revocation/new power of attorney and change of correspondence address with USPTO when representation changes
rubrics_metrics.description: When a practitioner takes over representation, the Revocation of Power of Attorney with a New Power of Attorney and Change of Correspondence Address should be filed with the USPTO to effect the change of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The failure to file the executed revocation/POA/change-of-address resulted in USPTO correspondence continuing to the former practitioner, contributing to abandonment of the application — the decision uses this as a factual basis for misconduct findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions factors — 37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b) (four-factor test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before imposing sanctions the Court must consider: (1) whether the practitioner violated a duty owed to a client/public/legal system/profession; (2) whether the practitioner acted intentionally, knowingly, or negligently; (3) the amount of actual or potential injury caused; and (4) existence of any aggravating or mitigating factors. 37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision applies these four factors: finding duty breaches to client and patent bar; concluding respondent acted knowingly/ intentionally; finding actual injury (lost/unreturned fees, abandoned application); and identifying aggravating factors (bad-faith obstruction, failing to appear) leading to exclusion from practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggravating factors (bad-faith obstruction, failure to appear) affecting sanction severity
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggravating circumstances include bad-faith obstruction of disciplinary proceedings (e.g., intentionally failing to respond to RFIs and court orders) and failure to appear, which can indicate inability to represent clients and support harsher sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision cites the American Bar Association's Standards for Imposing Lawyer Sanctions and treats respondent's intentional noncooperation and failure to appear as aggravating factors supporting exclusion from practice.
